questions.q: Per this lesson, what makes Lesson 25 different from the other 24 lessons in this course?
options: It isn't a new concept — it's the exercise that assembles the other 24 concepts into one program packet
It introduces an entirely new, previously untaught governance framework
It is the only lesson in the course that includes a quiz
It replaces the need for Chapters 1 through 4 entirely
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames itself as a synthesis exercise, not a twenty-fifth new concept.

questions.q: In the nine-step program packet, which chapter do steps 1 through 3 (charter, stakeholders, stewardship) come from?
options: Chapter 1 — Launching the Program
Chapter 3 — Measuring Governance
Chapter 5 — Sustaining Governance
Chapter 4 — Adoption and Change
questions.explain: The packet's first three steps map directly to Chapter 1's charter, stakeholder, and stewardship concepts.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about how many KPIs step 6 of the packet should name?
options: Exactly two, tied directly to the original pain the program solves — not a long vanity list
At least twenty, to cover every possible metric
Zero — KPIs are not part of the practice lab
As many as the governance council can think of in one meeting
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls for exactly two KPIs tied to the original pain, echoing Lesson 24's Brightfield Agritech example.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does it mean if a program's packet has solid steps 1-7 but step 8 (roadmap horizon placement) is the hard one?
options: The program is genuinely in the sustaining phase this chapter is about — basics are working, and the open question is sequencing and funding
The program should be shut down immediately
It means the charter and stewardship steps were done incorrectly
It means the program has no KPIs at all
questions.explain: The lesson uses exactly this diagnostic: strong fundamentals plus a hard roadmap/funding step signals a program in the sustaining phase, not a launch problem.

questions.q: What course does this lesson name as the next step in the Data Governance career path?
options: Data Governance Architecture
Data Governance Foundations
Metadata Management and Business Glossary
There is no next course — this is the final course in the path
questions.explain: The closing section explicitly names Data Governance Architecture as the next course in the path, moving from how a program is run to how the underlying systems are structured.
